By default, it MUST list matching definitions in full-name order when their evidence is missing, has a false determination, or fails the same evidence and reference checks as `habeas::validate()`. It MUST summarize FIXME judgments under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_summary`, with accepted FIXME subjects listed individually only when `--verbose` or `--all` is selected. `--all` MUST list every matching definition with its kind and evidence state. rationale:
**Verdict: the code implements `requirements.cli.status` and the tests cover its main cases.** I did not run the tests. I judged from the supplied source and test text.

**Implementation**
- `src/main.rs`, `Command::Status`, resolves the project root with `setup::project_root()`. It then calls `status_markdown_with_options(&root, all, glob, verbose)`. `main` is cited for both `cli.status` and `cli.fixme_summary`.
- Outside a Cargo and mdBook project, `project_root` fails with "cannot find a project with Cargo.toml and book.toml". This satisfies the "work from within a Cargo and mdBook project" and "report clearly" clauses.
- In `src/commands.rs`, `status_markdown_with_options` validates the glob through `definition_glob::validate`. An invalid glob such as `[` returns `InvalidInput` ("invalid definition glob").
- A valid glob that matches nothing returns `NotFound` ("no definitions match"). Term definitions are excluded from matching.
- With no glob, every requirement and example is considered.
- Definitions come from a `BTreeMap`, so they are visited in full-name order.
- For each definition it loads `LoadedDetailEvidence`, which gives one of Missing, Invalid, DeterminationFalse, Fixme or Valid. The state is derived from the shared `inspect_repository` report errors, so it uses the same checks as `validate()`.
- Valid rows are skipped unless `--all` is set. Fixme rows are skipped unless `--all` or `--verbose` is set. Other rows are listed with their kind and state.
- Per-definition findings are printed under "Validation findings". Report errors not tied to a listed definition are printed under "Other validation findings". Repository-wide Rust attestation findings therefore appear in every form, including when a glob is given.
- FIXME entries from every selected definition are collected into `FixmeSummary`, whatever the row filtering does. The summary is rendered with the `verbose` flag. The grouping details belong to `fixme_summary`, which has its own tests.

**Tests**
- `tests/commands.rs::status_lists_nonvalid_requirements_and_all_option_in_name_order`:
  - It runs from a nested `src/nested` directory.
  - It checks the Missing, Invalid (malformed JSON, stale text, stale input, uncovered reference) and Determination false states.
  - Valid rows are absent by default.
  - With `--all`, rows appear in name order, examples are labelled "(example)", and the Valid row is shown.
- `status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form` runs the four flag combinations (none, `--all`, `--verbose`, `--all --verbose`), each with and without a glob. It checks that "Other validation findings" and the Rust citation and attestation findings are always present.
- `commands_report_invalid_arguments_and_unmatched_selectors`:
  - Bad flags and extra arguments fail with a clap usage message.
  - A bad glob fails with "invalid definition glob".
  - An unmatched glob fails with "no definitions match".
  - The glob `requirements.*ready` selects the right subset with `--all`.
  - Running outside a project fails with the "cannot find a project" message.
- `status_groups_fixme_judgments_by_distinct_normalized_issue`, `verbose_status_lists_fixme_judgments_and_globs_scope_issue_groups` and `tests/outcomes.rs::valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book` cover the following:
  - FIXME rows are hidden by default.
  - FIXME rows appear with `--all` and `--verbose`.
  - The FIXME summary respects the glob.
  - HTML in FIXME text is escaped.
  - Valid FIXME judgments produce no validation findings.
- `tests/outcomes.rs` also covers a malformed FIXME shown as Invalid with its finding, and a stale input on a FIXME judgment still reporting its finding.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs` checks that status ignores an invalid user authoring configuration, which keeps it deterministic.

**Gaps**
I found no remaining gaps and no FIXME comments. The tests cover each obligation in the requirement text.

`habeas status` MUST group the selected requirement and example judgments marked
FIXME by issue reference and report how many distinct judgments each issue
affects. It MUST recognize `#123` and `owner/repo#123` within recorded FIXME
strings, including `FIXME(...)` and explanatory text. A GitHub issue URL such as
`https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123` MUST identify the same issue as
`owner/repo#123`. Issue numbers MUST be positive, complete numeric tokens with
leading zeros normalized; repository spelling MUST remain case-sensitive, and
unqualified and qualified references MUST remain distinct.
A judgment MUST count at most once for each issue, even when that issue occurs
repeatedly or in several FIXME strings. A judgment naming several issues MUST
count in each corresponding group. Judgments with no recognized issue in any
FIXME string MUST be counted once in a separate "FIXME without an issue" group.
Issue groups MUST be ordered by decreasing affected-judgment count, then by
normalized reference; the group without an issue MUST follow them. A supplied
glob MUST restrict these counts to the selected subjects.
`--verbose` MUST list the full name and kind of every judgment in each issue
group and in the group without an issue, along with its original FIXME strings.
The summary MUST include valid FIXME determinations even when other evidence
checks fail; grouping MUST NOT hide their validation findings. Malformed
determinations MUST remain validation errors under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.

Source files and book chapters can mark lines as implementing, citing, or testing a requirement or example:
Each reference must name an existing requirement or example. Its evidence must include an input covering the line with the reference. In the book, references and definitions become linked badges.

For Rust, Habeas parses first-party source files and requires every explicit function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, to have a requirement or named example reference in an attached comment or its body. Each named example cites a requirement. A reference on an enclosing `impl` or module, in a string literal, or only in an evidence input does not cover the function. A Rust source file that cannot be parsed is reported as an error. For a helper with no behavior-specific requirement, agree on an explicit project requirement such as `internal-detail` and provide evidence explaining why it adds no otherwise unspecified user-visible behavior.

Rust-item selectors use syntactic ancestry within one repository-relative file. Examples include `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`, `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`, `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`, and positional `use#1`. Duplicate sibling names gain `#1`, `#2`, and so on. Delimiter characters and whitespace within names or impl types use percent-encoded UTF-8 bytes, so spelling can be recovered without resolving modules across files. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`

Each Rust function also needs an attestation in `evidence/rust/<rust_file>.json`, with a `rust_file` field and a `functions` array. Every entry has `rust_item`, a `citations` array of `{ "role": "impl", "name": "requirements.some_name" }` objects, a boolean `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`. This determination assesses citation coverage; FIXME applies to requirement and example judgments. It needs one Rust-item input for that function and at least one requirements input covering every cited definition. The agent must review the whole function and relevant definitions, then explain why its citations include *every applicable* requirement or named example and how those texts account for its behavior together. A matching snapshot alone is insufficient. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_function_attestations` {cite}`requirements.cli.function_attestation_guidance`
